newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Podravka says soon to complete revamping.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Podravka says soon to complete revamping.

text.p: Croatia's largest food concern Podravka said on Wednesday it hoped to soon complete radical revamping, designed to set it on a path to profitability this year after piling losses.
"All the activities are now in a final phase. We have set a July 1 deadline to complete restructuring," public relations manager Zvonko Mrsic told Reuters by telephone.
Some personnel changes should also take place by this summer, he added but would not reveal other details.
However, his comments followed earlier announcements that the company, based in rural Podravina area of northern Croatia bordering Hungary, would gradually lay off workers.
Swapping out old debt raised at very high interest rates that have gnawed at its profits in recent years, for cheaper financing is also part of the plans to enable a healthy growth in the future.
Last year Podravka divested itself of five loss-making subsidiaries that had sunk it for the best part of the 135 million kuna group loss in 1995.
It has since engaged consultants Arthur D. Little to help it draw up new strategies. A new business plan will be ready for adoption by the end of this month, Mrsic said.
This paves the way for implementing a completely new marketing strategy, focused on boosting sales of key products such as the famous food seasoning Vegeta.
"Accounts for last year should also be finished by then and ready for auditing," he added, envisaging that the 1996 results will be available for release in the second half of May.
Podravka said it would seek a full listing on the Zagreb Stock Exchange, and possibly on another foreign bourse sometime later this year.
Its stock closed flat Wednesday at 305 kuna and was one of the most actively traded. Although slightly weaker than last week, it has risen from well below its 300 kuna face value in the past 10 days.
This movement has partly coincided with a government decision to slash to under four from 18 percent its stake in Podravka offered to beneficiaries of a mass privatisation.

The company's shares along with some 16 billion kuna worth of shares in other firms will be available in exchange for free vouchers from this autumn. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
